questions.stem: A 58-year-old Afro-Caribbean man attends his GP surgery for a routine health check. His clinic blood pressure is 152/94 mmHg. A repeat measurement 10 minutes later is 150/92 mmHg. Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) confirms an average daytime blood pressure of 146/90 mmHg. Urine dipstick is negative for protein, serum creatinine is 82 umol/L, and his 12-lead ECG is normal. According to UK clinical practice guidelines (NICE NG136), which of the following is the most appropriate initial pharmacological treatment?
questions.explanation: Under UK NICE NG136 guidelines, Step 1 antihypertensive treatment for adults aged 55 and over, or adults of any age of Black African or African-Caribbean family origin without type 2 diabetes, is a calcium channel blocker (CCB) such as amlodipine. ACE inhibitors or ARBs (ramipril or losartan) are preferred for non-Black individuals under 55 years of age. Beta-blockers (bisoprolol) are not routine first-line for uncomplicated hypertension unless there is another indication (e.g. angina, heart failure, or rate control in AF).
questions.learning_objective: Select appropriate Step 1 antihypertensive pharmacotherapy based on age and ethnicity per NICE NG136.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman is evaluated in the hypertension clinic for persistent severe hypertension. Her clinic blood pressure is 168/104 mmHg despite adhering to amlodipine 10 mg and ramipril 10 mg daily. Basic blood investigations reveal serum sodium 143 mmol/L, potassium 3.1 mmol/L (normal 3.5-5.0), and creatinine 74 umol/L. She takes no over-the-counter medications or herbal remedies. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial screening investigation for the suspected underlying cause of her secondary hypertension?
questions.explanation: The patient presents with treatment-resistant hypertension in a young adult accompanied by spontaneous hypokalemia (3.1 mmol/L), which strongly suggests primary aldosteronism (Conn's syndrome). The recommended initial screening test is the plasma aldosterone-to-renin ratio (ARR). Fractionated metanephrines screen for pheochromocytoma, which typically presents with paroxysmal headache, sweating, and palpitations. Renal Doppler evaluates renal artery stenosis, and urinary cortisol evaluates Cushing's syndrome.
questions.learning_objective: Identify the primary screening test for secondary hypertension caused by primary aldosteronism in a patient with hypokalemia.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old Caucasian man with newly diagnosed essential hypertension attends for medication review. His clinic blood pressure remains elevated at 158/98 mmHg despite 6 weeks of ramipril 5 mg once daily. He has no other comorbidities and normal renal function. In accordance with UK stepped-care guidance (NICE NG136), which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.text: Switch from ramipril to losartan 50 mg daily
Add a calcium channel blocker (e.g. amlodipine 5 mg daily)

questions.explanation: According to NICE NG136 stepped-care guidance for hypertension, when blood pressure is uncontrolled on Step 1 monotherapy with an ACE inhibitor (in a non-Black patient aged <55), Step 2 treatment is the combination of an ACE inhibitor (or ARB) with a calcium channel blocker (CCB). Switching to an ARB (losartan) is only indicated if the patient develops an intolerable dry cough on an ACE inhibitor. Spironolactone is used at Step 4 for resistant hypertension when potassium is <=4.5 mmol/L. Doxazosin is an alternative Step 4 alpha-blocker.
questions.learning_objective: Recognize Step 2 combination therapy (ACEi/ARB plus CCB) in the NICE NG136 hypertension treatment algorithm.

She is asymptomatic with a heart rate of 78 beats/min. Her blood pressure is 134/82 mmHg, and echocardiography shows mild left atrial enlargement with a normal left ventricular ejection fraction (58%). She has no prior history of stroke, thromboembolism, or bleeding. According to UK clinical practice guidelines (NICE NG196), which of the following is the most appropriate stroke prevention strategy?

choices.text: Dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel

questions.explanation: This patient's CHA2DS2-VASc score is 4 (Age 65-74 = 1, Female sex = 1, Hypertension = 1, Diabetes = 1). Aspirin or antiplatelet therapy is explicitly contraindicated as sole therapy for stroke prevention in AF due to lack of efficacy and similar bleeding risk.

On examination, he has a new harsh 3/6 pansystolic murmur at the cardiac apex and splinter hemorrhages in his nailbeds. Infective endocarditis is suspected. Urine antigen test for Legionella pneumophila

questions.stem: A 74-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after experiencing a syncopal episode while walking in her garden. On examination, her heart rate is 34 bpm, and blood pressure is 88/54 mmHg. She feels dizzy and appears pale and diaphoretic. A 12-lead ECG demonstrates complete atrioventricular block (third-degree AV block) with a ventricular escape rate of 34 bpm. Adenosine, beta-blockers, and verapamil further suppress AV conduction and are contraindicated.

questions.stem: An 80-year-old man receives a standard dual-chamber pacemaker with right ventricular apical pacing (RVAP) for symptomatic high-grade AV block. One year later, he develops new exertional dyspnoea and bilateral leg edema. Echocardiogram reveals that his left ventricular ejection fraction has declined from 55% to 35% with marked intraventricular dyssynchrony. Which of the following long-term adverse effects of conventional right ventricular apical pacing explains this presentation?

choices.text: Pacing-induced cardiomyopathy due to ventricular dyssynchrony

questions.explanation: Right ventricular apical pacing (RVAP) induces an artificial left bundle branch block activation pattern, causing ventricular dyssynchrony, asymmetrical hypertrophy, and impaired left ventricular systolic function, termed pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. This occurs in 10–20% of patients with high percentages of RV apical pacing, prompting the development of physiological conduction system pacing techniques.
questions.learning_objective: Identify pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and ventricular dyssynchrony as potential complications of RV apical pacing.

citations.quote: Right ventricular apical pacing (RVAP) is the most common ventricular pacing site. However, it can be associated with ventricular desynchrony, pacing induced cardiomyopathy and impaired ventricular function [ 1 ].

Continuous-wave Doppler across the aortic valve demonstrates a peak aortic jet velocity (Vmax) of 4.3 m/s and a mean transvalvular pressure gradient of 44 mmHg. questions.explanation: In functional (secondary) mitral regurgitation (FMR), the mitral valve leaflets and chordae tendineae are structurally normal. questions.stem: A 71-year-old woman with chronic ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 28%) is admitted for worsening pulmonary edema. Echocardiography shows severe functional mitral regurgitation secondary to left ventricular spherical remodeling. She is currently taking ramipril 2.5 mg and furosemide 40 mg daily. According to NICE heart failure guidelines (NG106) and valvular guidelines (NG208), what is the mandatory first-line strategy before considering invasive transcatheter or surgical mitral valve interventions for secondary/functional MR?

choices.text: Immediate urgent open-heart mechanical mitral valve replacement
High-dose oral steroid therapy for six months
Discontinuation of all ACE inhibitors and beta-blockers
Optimization of guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

questions.explanation: In functional mitral regurgitation (FMR), guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (including ACEi/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, and SGLT2i, plus cardiac resynchronization therapy if indicated) is the essential first-line foundation. Optimal medical therapy promotes reverse LV remodeling and can substantially diminish the severity of functional regurgitation. Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) or surgery is considered only if severe symptomatic MR persists despite optimal GDMT.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man with severe ischemic functional mitral regurgitation refractory to optimal medical therapy is discussed in the Heart Team meeting. The cardiac surgeons and cardiologists consider whether restrictive mitral valve annuloplasty repair or mitral valve replacement is more suitable. According to surgical series evaluating functional mitral regurgitation outcomes, what is the primary long-term clinical challenge associated with restrictive annuloplasty repair in patients with severe LV tethering and adverse remodeling?

choices.text: High rate of recurrent mitral regurgitation over long-term follow-up
Ineffectiveness of all subsequent oral diuretics
Requirement for lifelong high-dose warfarin anticoagulation

questions.explanation: The major limitation of restrictive mitral valve annuloplasty repair in functional mitral regurgitation is a significant rate of recurrent mitral regurgitation (observed in up to 30–50% of patients within 2 years in randomized CTSN trials), primarily driven by ongoing left ventricular remodeling and progressive leaflet tethering. Despite this risk, repair avoids prosthetic valve-related complications and has been associated with favorable operative recovery in selected cohorts.
